response.title: what is the best balcony solar kit for an apartment renter
response.answer:
For an apartment renter, the best balcony solar kit is one that's removable, safe to mount without drilling, and capable of delivering useful electricity without permanent modifications.

There are two very different types of balcony solar systems:

Plug-in balcony solar: Sends electricity into your apartment's electrical system to reduce your utility bill. Popular in Europe, but subject to stricter rules and compatibility requirements in the US.

Portable solar + battery: Stores solar energy in a portable power station for running electronics and small appliances. Usually the more renter-friendly option in the US.

If you're renting in California, I'd lean toward a portable solar-and-battery system unless you've confirmed that a grid-connected balcony system is permitted by your landlord, utility, and local electrical rules.

My top picks

Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 Portable Power Station with 100W Bif…

$709.99

At B&H Photo

1,024Wh battery, 2,000W AC output, and a 100W solar panel. Good for apartment backup and daily device charging, though I'd prefer a larger panel for meaningful daily solar generation.

View kit

Shop

$749.00

At Course & Trail

1,070Wh battery with a 200W folding panel. A stronger solar-panel pairing for a sunny balcony, provided there's enough space to deploy it.

View kit

These are portable off-grid systems, not plug-in kits that directly offset your apartment's meter.

Important California update

California passed SB 868 in September 2026. Starting January 1, 2027, qualifying plug-in balcony solar systems up to 1,200W AC can operate without traditional utility interconnection approval. However, certification requirements still apply, and landlord permission remains a separate issue. As of late October, compliant products had not yet received approval. 
LegiScan
+1

If your primary goal is reducing your electric bill, rather than backup power, I would wait for certified plug-in kits instead of spending $700–$1,000 on a battery system.

This distinction matters because the best system for electricity savings can be completely different from the best portable solar generator.
